segments.title: Chương 308: 0310【Game di động quốc dân】
segments.content:
"Ding-a-ling!"

Chen Guiliang once again rode his bicycle, ringing the bell as he made his way through the campus.

He was going to take his final exams.

He hadn't spent much time on campus this semester, nor had he been back to his dorm much.

The daily affairs of his two companies, the preparations for ByteDance's IPO, practicing English in his spare time, and occasionally getting together with Bian Guanyue and Tao Xue on weekends left Chen Guiliang with no time to attend to school matters.

He had just finished one exam in the morning, and right after the submission deadline, Director Zhu called him right on the dot.

Chen Guiliang rode his bicycle again, heading to Director Zhu's office.

Director Zhu joked, "CEO Chen, you're usually so busy, I didn't dare to call. I had to seize the opportunity during your final exams."

"Then I've troubled Director Zhu to look up my exam schedule," Chen Guiliang played along with a grin.

"Have a seat. I'll go make some tea for CEO Chen."

"Thank you for your trouble."

The teacher and student had a pretty good relationship, to the point where they could casually joke around in private.

Chen Guiliang really did just sit there, waiting for Director Zhu to bring over the tea.

As he took the teacup, he handed Director Zhu a Zhonghua cigarette.

Director Zhu put the cigarette down and said, "The Yuanpei Program is about to be upgraded to Yuanpei College. The official founding ceremony for the college will be held when the new students start school. I'll be the first dean."

"Congratulations, congratulations!" Chen Guiliang immediately offered his congratulations.

This Director Zhu had finally made it after all these years.

His current title was "Deputy Director of the Yuanpei Program Management Committee," and he had been responsible for all aspects of the Yuanpei Program for many years. As for the Director of the Yuanpei Management Committee, it was an honorary position held by the university president.

Director Zhu was clearly in an excellent mood, accepting Chen Guiliang's congratulations with a beaming smile. He then added, "The college's founding ceremony will be held at the same time as the new students' opening ceremony. If you have time then, you can represent the Yuanpei students and give a speech on stage."

Chen Guiliang said, "If it doesn't clash with a certain event, I'll definitely give a speech."

What was this certain event?

An IPO roadshow or the listing ceremony bell-ringing!

Director Zhu was a little surprised. Based on his understanding of Chen Guiliang, it was unlikely he would turn down something like this. He asked curiously, "Does your company have something important going on? Of course, you don't have to say if it's not convenient."

Chen Guiliang said, "It's really not convenient to say. The moment I say it, it would be a violation of regulations."

Director Zhu instantly guessed it might be about going public, so he smiled and said, "Then I'll also wish you the best of luck with your event."

"Thanks to Director Zhu's... no, Dean Zhu's auspicious words," Chen Guiliang began to change his form of address.

Director Zhu waved his hand and said, "You should still call me Director or Teacher."

"After the college is established, will we have to change dorms?" Chen Guiliang inquired. He was asking on behalf of the other students.

Director Zhu said, "Everyone will move into Building 43. Although the other conditions are similar, it has been renovated to have shower rooms on each floor, so you won't have to go downstairs and queue up for a shower anymore."

These living conditions were still a far cry from the Yuanpei dorms of a decade later. Back then, they directly renovated two basement floors, creating an exclusive library, conference rooms, a movie theater, a gym, a coffee bar, piano rooms... and even offices for counselors and tutors right in the dormitory building.

Chen Guiliang continued to chat idly with Director Zhu for a while. It was almost time for lunch, so he bid farewell and rode his bike to the cafeteria.

It had been a long time since he'd eaten at the school cafeteria, and he actually missed it a bit.

Along the way, students would occasionally greet Chen Guiliang, teasing him about making ill-gotten gains from the graduating students.

"Chen Guiliang!"

A girl shouted in a startled manner.

Chen Guiliang took a closer look, but he had no impression of her at all. Still, he responded with a smile.

The girl, however, stopped Chen Guiliang and turned her head to shout, "Dad, Mom, I ran into Chen Guiliang!"

Immediately, a middle-aged couple walked over from under the trees by the road.

Chen Guiliang had a rough idea of who they were.

The girl said, "I'm a college entrance exam taker from Su Province this year, and I really admire you. I want to apply for Peking University's Yuanpei Program too!"

This young lady seemed very confident. It had only been a week since the Gaokao, and she didn't even know her score yet, but she was already certain she wanted to apply to Peking University. And specifically, Peking University's Yuanpei Program.

Chen Guiliang wondered if he should apply for the title of "Yuanpei Program Image Ambassador" the next time he saw Director Zhu. With him as the face of the program, Director Zhu's student recruitment would be even easier.

The girl's parents also sized up Chen Guiliang, and the more they looked, the more spirited the young man appeared.

They held Chen Guiliang up, chatting for quite a while.

Chen Guiliang used the excuse of being hungry to end the conversation and go to the cafeteria to eat. But the family was exceptionally enthusiastic, insisting on treating him to a meal at a restaurant outside.

They were clearly wealthy; otherwise, the parents wouldn't be accompanying their daughter on a tour of a university campus just after she finished the Gaokao.

Chen Guiliang politely declined and pedaled his bike toward the cafeteria.

"This young man is really accomplished for his age. I heard his company has become very large."

"And he's so handsome. I wonder if he has a girlfriend."

"He must. A young man like him is very popular at school."

"Not necessarily. He might be too busy with his career to have time for romance."

In the eyes of many parents, Chen Guiliang had become the quintessential "child of other people," with an absolutely positive and upright image.

Arriving at the cafeteria, Chen Guiliang got his food, found a seat, and watched "Legal Report Today" with great interest.

As he watched, he started to feel a bit displeased; it really soured his mood.

A driver had repeatedly run over an elderly person five times, causing their death, and then disappeared after providing 80,000 yuan for medical expenses. Because it couldn't be proven that there was "subjective intent to kill," he was ultimately only sentenced to three years and ordered to pay the family 550,000 yuan in compensation.

Sigh, can't they broadcast some more cheerful news?

Chen Guiliang buried his head in his food. A discussion had already started in the cafeteria, the focal point of the debate being whether there was an intent to kill. The driver insisted he hadn't seen the person, thinking he had run over a trash bag on the side of the road when reversing. But why would he repeatedly run over a trash bag?

"Chen Guiliang, do you think he should be sentenced to death?" a student eating at the same table asked.

Chen Guiliang didn't know this person either, but he nodded and said, "He should!"

The student continued, "Being able to produce 80,000 yuan for medical expenses and then pay 550,000 in compensation to the family shows the driver must be a rich man. I reckon the driver pulled some strings, otherwise there's no way he would only get three years."

Chen Guiliang smiled and didn't reply.

The student then started chatting with other students, each one filled with righteous indignation.

That afternoon, several blog posts on HaiNei.com shot into the top 20 most-read list site-wide. All of them were related to the case from "Legal Report Today."

Although HaiNei.com's content moderation was relatively strict, it still attracted a large number of opinion leaders whose articles keenly captured various current hot topics. This could greatly increase user activity and website traffic.

It was estimated that with this year's "South China Tiger Photo Scandal" and next year's "Sanlu Melamine Scandal," HaiNei.com would also become a very lively place.

There were no exams in the afternoon, so Chen Guiliang returned to the company to arrange for the response to this round of inquiries. After each round of inquiries, ByteDance had one to two weeks to resolve various issues.

His phone rang.

Chen Guiliang answered it and put it to his ear, but was instantly blasted with noise and had to move the phone a little farther away.

Several people were cheering and shouting on the phone. Tang Kai, the CEO of Dingguo Technology, exclaimed wildly, "CEO Chen, our 'Seven Nights' has been nominated for the IMGA Best 3D Game award! This is the first game from all of China, including Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan, to be nominated for an IMGA award!"

Chen Guiliang, who wasn't familiar with early mobile games, was a little stunned by this news. But even more so, he was pleasantly surprised.

The founders sent several emails begging for help, I casually invested a sum of money, and then this company's product gets nominated for the most authoritative international mobile game award?

This was too outrageous.

He didn't know, however, that if he hadn't invested, these seven young men wouldn't even have been able to scrape together the travel expenses to attend the awards ceremony. They had posted pleas for help everywhere, but not a single company was willing to help them.

Chen Guiliang went downstairs to Game Science, called Qu Guohao over, and said, "Dingguo Technology, which we invested in at the beginning of the year, their game 'Seven Nights' has been nominated for the IMGA Best 3D Game award."

Qu Guohao looked bewildered, "What's IMGA?"

Chen Guiliang laughed, "Even you don't know, so I'm afraid the vast majority of domestic game companies don't know either. I asked Tang Kai in detail. IMGA stands for International Mobile Gaming Awards, an award specifically for mobile games. This year's ceremony is in Cannes, France, the same place that holds the film festival."

"The most authoritative mobile game award?" Qu Guohao asked.

Chen Guiliang nodded, "It is indeed the most authoritative in the world. Even if it's not, we can promote it as authoritative. When you do the promotion, use slogans like 'the Oscars of the mobile game industry' or something similar. Anyway, hype it up as much as possible, and then launch 'Seven Nights' for sale in the process!"

Qu Guohao said, "Should we sell it before the awards ceremony, or after?"

Chen Guiliang said, "It's just a nomination, winning will be very difficult. The other four nominated games are surely incredible too. So, you also have to promote the strength of our competitors to encourage domestic players to buy and support it. If we don't win, we'll focus on promoting how amazing the winner is, giving domestic players a sense of 'glorious defeat'."

"So we release it before the official awards ceremony?" Qu Guohao understood.

Chen Guiliang said, "Game Science will send a few people to cover the awards ceremony on-site, and while they're at it, import those nominated games. Very few people in China pay attention to this award, so we probably won't have much competition."

Qu Guohao said, "Licensing top foreign mobile games must be expensive, right?"

"Bargain them down, just say we're the only ones willing to buy," Chen Guiliang suggested.

Although Game Science was also making small mobile games, when it came to actual distribution, they still had to cooperate with HaiNei.com's WAP site. Because the Game Science platform was on PC, no one would download mobile games there.

The only one truly making big money from mobile games at the moment was KongZhong Corporation, which had a massive number of mobile internet users.

However, they could use this nomination to let more netizens learn about mobile games and take the opportunity to build up the mobile game channel on the Game Science platform.

Several days later.

Promotional articles appeared all over Xiaonei.com and HaiNei.com, and a large number of paid posters went to forums and Tieba to post.

"Game Science's subsidiary, Dingguo Technology's product 'Seven Nights,' has been nominated for this year's IMGA Best 3D Game... IMGA is known as the Oscars and Golden Globes of the mobile game industry. Since the award's inception, this is the first time a work from a Chinese-speaking region has been nominated..."

"Chinese game developers are in no way inferior to those in Europe, America, Japan, and Korea. We can also produce works that will stun the world... It is reported that before Game Science invested in Dingguo Technology, this small company consisted of only seven young men who resolutely quit their jobs to pursue their dream, working day and night on development without pay..."

"After the company's funds were exhausted, they survived on instant noodles every day, constantly seeking help from major companies in the industry... Chen Guiliang, the founder of Game Science, received multiple letters of appeal from them and was moved by their spirit..."

"After 'Seven Nights' was submitted to the IMGA, jury members from many countries around the world were utterly shocked by this game. They could not imagine that such a good mobile game existed in China... The IMGA's Best 3D Game award carries immense weight, representing the highest level of technology in the mobile gaming world..."

Hype it up, hype it up big!

One promotional article after another was published, leaving netizens deeply moved and their blood boiling with excitement.

A sense of national pride surged up at once.

Their industry peers, however, were completely baffled. What the heck is IMGA? Why haven't we heard of it before?

Oh right, "Seven Nights" hadn't applied for a publication number yet.

Chen Guiliang called Director Kou. As soon as Director Kou heard that it had been nominated for an international award, he immediately gave personal instructions to the relevant personnel to expedite the approval process.

Moreover, the publication administration was also going to send officials to attend the awards ceremony.
